turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_target.csv: 229 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below, within each
observed range, whose critical temperature Tc (K) is AS CLOSE AS POSSIBLE to
90. Design variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])
  - Y (fraction in [0, 0.4])
  - Ca (fraction in [0, 0.272727])
  - La (fraction in [0, 0.78])
  - Bi (fraction in [0, 0.521978])
  - Fe (fraction in [0, 0.502513])
  - Nb (fraction in [0, 0.98])
  - C (fraction in [0, 0.972])
  - Pr (fraction in [0, 0.265043])
  - As (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - B (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Pb (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - Ce (fraction in [0, 0.28])
  - Mo (fraction in [0, 1])
  - V (fraction in [0, 0.9918])
  - Zn (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Ni (fraction in [0, 0.6])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: O=0.348837, Cu=0.227273, Ba=0.166667, Sr=0.142857, Y=0.2,
Ca=0.136364, La=0.39, Bi=0.260989, Fe=0.251256, Nb=0.49, C=0.486,

turns.answer_text:
The training data has a gap around 90 K for compositions using only the allowed elements: Y/Ca/Ba/La cuprates reach roughly 60–67 K, while the allowed Bi–Sr–Ca–Cu–O entry `Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10` is 110 K. A reasonable target-90 proposal is therefore an interpolation between those two allowed-element cuprate families, avoiding low-Tc elements such as Fe, Nb, C, As, B, Mo, V, Zn, Ni.

Using about 46.5% of the 67 K `Y0.6Ca0.4Ba1.2La0.8Cu3O7.15` composition and 53.5% of the 110 K `Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10` composition gives normalized fractions near Tc ≈ 90 K.
